garrick.s2: garrick[businesslike]: Captain! Garrick Grumblegut, reporting for piracy. I've been familiarising myself with the assets.
garrick[greedy]: All of them, Captain. Due diligence.
garrick.s3: garrick[pretend]: Afternoon, Captain. Lovely weather. Quiet weather. Nothing rumbling in it whatsoever.

then: garrick[worried]: Captain, whatever you do down there, don't linger in the thick of it. The Dead Center is... well. It's the premium product.
garrick[nervous]: And watch your boots. I say that as a friend. And as a man who has ruined a great many boots.
else: garrick[worried]: Captain, whatever happens, nobody goes near the middle of it.
garrick[businesslike]: I'm not being modest. It's a professional warning.

garrick.s5: garrick[nervous]: How is the bird, Captain? I'd like to send a card.
garrick[businesslike]: I'll sign it from 'the crew'. Plausible deniability.
garrick.s6: garrick[worried]: The crew are looking at me the way my creditors used to, Captain.
garrick[pretend]: My creditors are also why I was in a bathtub. Unrelated. Mostly.
garrick.tr: garrick[nervous]: Captain, as a valued employee, I'd like to request representation. Anyone at all.
garrick.frigate_helm: garrick[businesslike]: The helm, Captain! Put us upwind of them.
garrick[greedy]: The wind does the delivery. We just open the package.
garrick.frigate_sail: garrick[greedy]: The line by the foremast, Captain! One pull and the whole pocket goes over.
garrick[businesslike]: Premium grade. I'd put my name on it. I have, in a sense.
garrick.s8_1: garrick[businesslike]: Captain! I've drafted a proposal. 'Grumblegut Maritime Deterrence, Limited.'
garrick[greedy]: Ships pay us not to sail upwind of them. Recurring revenue.
garrick: I'll put you down as 'considering it'.
garrick.s8_2: garrick[relieved]: The rowboat's rather peaceful, Captain. I've started calling it my satellite office.
garrick.s8_3: garrick[pretend]: No, Captain. That wasn't me. That was the hull. Settling.
garrick[nervous]: Please don't call the bird.
garrick.s8_4: garrick[greedy]: I've been appraising the treasure again. Still worthless.
garrick[delighted]: But the smell is holding its value beautifully.
squawks.s2: squawks[insulting]: SQUAWK! The bathtub man owes me a biscuit! He took it! He called it a 'loan'!
squawks[smug]: Captain, I've been thinking. Throw him back. SQUAWK.
squawks.s3: squawks[worried]: Captain. Captain. His belly. It spoke.
squawks[horrified]: It spoke in a language only the damned understand. SQUAWK.
squawks.s5: squawks[exhausted]: Don't look at me. Don't LOOK at me.
squawks[outraged]: I had a CREST, Captain! A MAGNIFICENT crest! Now I have THREE FEATHERS and a GRUDGE!
squawks.s6: squawks[furious]: Hang him! Keelhaul him! Put him in a rowboat and push it into the SUN! SQUAWK!
squawks.tr: squawks[outraged]: Don't say anything about the sweater. Mags made it. It is WARM. That is ALL.
squawks.s8_1: squawks[smug]: SQUAWK! Captain, I've perfected the warning. Listen.
squawks.s8_2: squawks: My feathers are coming back. Slowly. I have four now.
squawks.s8_3: squawks[insulting]: If the businessman so much as HICCUPS, I'm sounding the alarm. SQUAWK.

start: bob[happy]: Morning, Cap'n! Want a sip?
bob[happy]: I know! Tastes like spicy sunshine!

then: bob[happy]: Like a warm day, but on fire! Doc says it'll make me glow. I'm hoping for green.

start: captain[annoyed]: Back in the lantern, Bob. All of it.
bob[sad]: Yes, Cap'n. Mostly all of it.

bob.s1: bob[happy]: I put it back in the lantern, Cap'n! Most of it!
bob: The lantern's burning ever so cheerful now.
bob.s2: bob[happy]: The bathtub man says I've got a head for business!
bob: Then he asked if he could borrow it.
bob.s3: bob: Cap'n, I heard his tummy! Sounded like my tummy after the lamp oil!
bob[happy]: Maybe HE drank lamp oil! We should compare!
bob.s4: bob[coughing]: Cap'n, it smells like the time I ate a candle! Only... more!
bob.s5: bob[sad]: Squawks is all pink now, Cap'n. Like a baby.
bob: A really, really angry baby.
bob.s6: bob: If the gold's ruined, can I have some? I'll take the stinkiest bit. I don't mind. Haven't had a nose since Tuesday.
bob.tr: bob[happy]: I'm on the jury! What are we deciding? Is it lunch?
bob.s8_1: bob[happy]: I asked if I could go in the rowboat too, Cap'n. They said I haven't earned it.
bob.s8_2: bob: Garrick says his stomach is a 'proprietary weather system'.
ned.s1: ned: Morning, Captain. Back on watch after the ague. One eye, all of it on the horizon.
ned.s2: ned: Spotted him at a mile off, Captain. Thought he was a buoy.
ned: Still not convinced he isn't.
ned.s3: ned[concerned]: Heard something from below, Captain. Checked the horizon for weather.
ned: Weather's fine. Weather isn't the problem.
ned.s4: ned[coughing]: Can't see a thing in this, Captain. And I only had the one to start with.
ned.s5: ned: Eye on the horizon, back to the hatch. Best arrangement on the ship right now.
ned.s6: ned: Sail on the horizon earlier, Captain. A merchant.
ned: The wind shifted and she turned away so hard she nearly capsized. Can't blame her.
ned.tr: ned: Navy colours, forty guns, and a captain who thinks he's having a good day.
ned.s8_1: ned: Nobody comes near us now, Captain. Merchants, navy, gulls.
ned[smug]: Never had such an empty horizon. It's restful.
ned.s8_2: ned: When the rowboat's out, I keep an eye on it.
ned: From a distance. The distance is the important part.

then: jim: Captain. Salting's done, every barrel in the forepeak full to the lid. So I'm back on the galley, and Mags has someone to shout at who isn't Quill.
jim: Pickled onions, pickled eggs, pickled herring. Mind the crocks on that shelf. Some of them are older than Wick.
else: jim: Something needs pickling, Captain? Everything needs pickling, eventually.

jim.s2: jim[annoyed]: Your new man came sniffing round my crocks, Captain. Said he was 'surveying the inventory'.
jim: I told him the inventory bites.
jim.s3: jim[concerned]: Twelve onions, Captain. Twelve. And the eel paste.
jim: I've kept that jar sealed eleven years. Eleven years.
jim.s4: jim[coughing]: The eel paste. I knew it. I KNEW it. Eleven years that jar sat quiet, and one afternoon with him...
jim.s5: jim: I've written a new label for the eel paste. It says 'NO.'
jim: I've put it on every jar aboard, to be safe.
jim.s6: jim[annoyed]: Worthless, Captain? The whole hold? Then I'll pickle it.
jim: Pickled gold. Somebody'll buy anything if it's pickled.
jim.tr: jim: Add a fifth charge, Captain: stealing bait. Put it at the top.
jim.s8_1: jim: New galley rules. Mister Grumblegut eats last, eats light, and eats on deck.
jim[angry]: And never, EVER anything out of a jar.
jim.s8_2: jim[happy]: I kept one of those old sausages, Captain. Not for eating.
jim: It's nailed over the stove. As a warning.

then: penhallow[annoyed]: Captain. Aldous Penhallow, of Penhallow and Daughters, cloth and fine goods. I wish to register a complaint.
penhallow: The hammock. The stew. The chain. And a man called Bob, who keeps asking to borrow my spectacles to look at the sun.
captain: Your ransom letter went out with the last ship. Your daughters will pay.
penhallow[offended]: My daughters are the ones who suggested I travel.
else: penhallow[annoyed]: I'd like it noted that the chain chafes, Captain. I would like it noted in ink.

penhallow.s2: penhallow: I hear you've taken on another passenger, Captain. Does he get a chain too?
penhallow[offended]: I'd like it noted that mine is too tight.
penhallow.s3: penhallow[alarmed]: Captain, the deck just shook. Is the ship sinking?
penhallow: I haven't been ransomed yet. It would be such a waste.
penhallow.s4: penhallow[coughing]: Captain! Unchain me! I'll pay! I'll pay my own ransom!
penhallow[terrified]: Then I'll pay for a WINDOW!
penhallow.s5: penhallow[disgusted]: I have lived in a hammock for nine days, Captain. I thought I knew what a bad smell was.
penhallow.s6: penhallow[disgusted]: I stand by my appraisal, Captain. Not one coin.
penhallow: I'd sooner be paid in herring. Pickled herring. From that nice man's jars.
penhallow.tr: penhallow: I hear there's to be a trial. If he's found guilty, can he have my chain?
penhallow.s8_1: penhallow[smug]: A ship that smells like this cannot be boarded, Captain.
penhallow: As a merchant, I resent it. As a prisoner, I find it oddly reassuring.
penhallow.s8_2: penhallow: My daughters wrote. They've heard about the smell.
penhallow[offended]: They've doubled the ransom. On condition that you keep me.
